key_insight: SqDRIFT-AIMD combines sampling-based quantum diagonalization with analytical nuclear gradients to extend quantum-centric molecular dynamics beyond active spaces tractable by exact diagonalization.
engineering_relevance: The approach advances quantum-assisted prediction of molecular motion by improving electronic energies while maintaining accurate proton-transfer dynamics and stable total energy.
method: Use randomized sample-based Krylov quantum diagonalization (SqDRIFT) to estimate ground-state electronic energies.
Combine SqDRIFT with analytical nuclear gradients to propagate molecular dynamics.
Execute quantum circuits on IBM Heron r3 processors to study proton transfer in the Zundel cation.
evidence_signal: At 40 qubits, SqDRIFT energies fall below CCSD across the double-well potential, the trajectory tracks SHCI-driven proton transfer within 1.33 mÅ, and total-energy standard deviation is 0.245 mEh; at 52 qubits, energies remain within a few mEh of CCSD.
watch_item: The abstract demonstrates dynamics at 40 qubits and energy calculations at 52 qubits, but does not establish end-to-end computational advantage or scaling to larger molecular systems.
paper_title: Towards large-scale ab initio Molecular Dynamics Simulation with Efficient Sampling-based Quantum Computing Algorithms
